Which is the best AI engineering course or bootcamp in India for freshers, with live classes?

Searched the web

There’s no single best option, and most of the “top 10” lists I found are not neutral. Several are published by the course sellers themselves. LogicMojo, for example, ranks its own course #1 across multiple pages, and Shifttotech advertises “100% placement support.” Treat placement percentages and rankings on those pages as marketing. Even one of the lists notes that no programme on it guarantees a job. logicmojo

Live-class options that came up (fees are as the sellers state them):

  • Futurense x IITM Pravartak: a live online program built with IIT Madras’s technology hub, aimed at freshers and working professionals, covering context engineering, applied AI, ML and deep learning. futurense
  • Masai / IIT Patna (Vishlesan i-Hub) program: 9 months, live online classes with a capstone, about 10 hours a week, open to 12th pass and above, with placement support only for those with 7+ CGPA and 65% attendance. masaischool
  • Scaler AI/ML track: ₹3–3.5 lakh, 11–14 months, live online. logicmojo
  • TalentSprint: ₹2.5–4 lakh+, 8–12 months, positioned as a premium option with strong interview prep. logicmojo
  • LogicMojo: ₹65,000, 6–9 months, live online, with a self-reported 87% placement rate. That figure comes from its own site, so verify it independently. logicmojo
  • Shifttotech: ₹35,000 live weekend batches. This is the cheapest live option, but I couldn’t find independent evidence of its quality. shifttotech

How I’d choose between them:

  1. Attend a free demo class and ask to talk to alumni from the last 1–2 batches.
  2. Check that the curriculum goes beyond prompts into RAG, evaluation, agents and deployment. One guide argues a 2026 AI course without prompt engineering and RAG pipelines isn’t worth it. futurense
  3. Ask for placement data you can verify, such as named companies, LinkedIn profiles of alumni, and the roles they got, not just a percentage.
  4. Check the refund policy and whether live sessions are recorded.

My view: if you can already build software, a ₹3 lakh bootcamp is probably more than you need. Employers increasingly care about whether you can build and deploy AI systems, and a bootcamp certificate won’t count for much with employers outside India. A cheaper path is a structured course such as DeepLearning.AI or the IBM certificate on Coursera, plus 2–3 deployed projects on AWS or GCP. If you want live accountability, a mid-priced cohort with a good demo class is enough. The ₹3 lakh programs mainly buy mentorship and interview prep, so they’re worth it mainly if you want that structure.

If you tell me your budget and whether you’re aiming for a job in India or abroad, I can narrow this to two or three options.
